hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 1]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 2]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

This means that the line of reflection is the line that contains the midpoints between corresponding points of the pre-image and image.

options.definition: The figure *after* one or more transformations

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
We could pick any pairs of corresponding points to help us find the line of reflection. 

First, let's find the midpoint between $\blueD{A(-4,-4)}$ and $\maroonD{A'(-6,-2)}$.

$\left( \dfrac{\blueD{-4}+\maroonD{(-6)}}{2}, \dfrac{\blueD{-4}+\maroonD{(-2)}}{2}\right)=(-5,-3)$



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle ABC and triangle A prime B prime C prime are drawn. Triangle ABC has point A at negative four, negative four, point B at negative one, negative one, point C at three, negative two. Triangle A prime, B prime, C prime has point A prime at negative six, negative two, point B prime at negative three, one, and point C prime at negative four, five. There is a plotted point at negative five, negative three at the endpoint of one line segment connected to A and another line segment connected to A prime. These line segments are congruent.

hints.content:
We could find the line that passes through $(-5,-3)$ and is perpendicular to the segment $\overline{AA'}$, or we could find a second midpoint.

Let's find the midpoint between $\blueD{B(-1,-1)}$ and $\maroonD{B'(-3,1)}$.

$\left( \dfrac{\blueD{-1}+\maroonD{(-3)}}{2}, \dfrac{\blueD{-1}+\maroonD{1}}{2}\right)=(-2,0)$



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle ABC and triangle A prime B prime C prime are drawn. Triangle ABC has point A at negative four, negative four, point B at negative one, negative one, point C at three, negative two. Triangle A prime, B prime, C prime has point A prime at negative six, negative two, point B prime at negative three, one, and point C prime at negative four, five. There is a plotted point at negative two, zero at the endpoint of one line segment connected to B and another line segment connected to B prime. These line segments are congruent.

hints.content:
The line shown here passes through both midpoints and is perpendicular to $\overline{AA'}$ and $\overline{BB'}$. So it is the line of reflection.



[[☃ image 1]]

Triangle A prime, B prime, C prime has point A prime at negative six, negative two, point B prime at negative three, one, and point C prime at negative four, five. There is a plotted point at negative five, negative three at the endpoint of one line segment connected to A and another line segment connected to A prime. These line segments are congruent. There is another plotted point at negative two, zero at the endpoint of one line segment connected to B and another line segment connected to B prime. These line segments are congruent. A line passes through both plotted points.
